full_judgment:
Md Abdul Quddus J: Criminal Appeal No. 1448 of 1993 by convict-appellant Mujibul Haque @ Mujibur Rahman and Criminal Appeal No. 1685 of 1993 by convict-appellants Abdul Hakim @ Henju and Md Ismail are directed against judgment, order of conviction and sentence dated 15-7-1993 by Sessions Judge Feni in Sessions Case 18 of 1992 arising out of Dagoan Bhuiyan PS Case 1 dated 10-10-1991 GR Case 53 of 1991 under sections 302/34 Penal Code. 

 9. Being aggrieved by the impugned judgment, order of conviction and sentence as above the convict-appellant Mozibul Haque @ Mojibur Rahman preferred Criminal Appeal No. 1448 of 1993 and convict-appellants Abdul Hakim Henju and Md Ismail preferred Criminal Appeal No. 1685 of 1993. Against the acquittal order the State preferred Criminal Appeal No. 4 of 1994. All the above appeals were heard together and disposed of by same judgment, which will govern all above appeals. 

 10. Learned Advocate for appellant Mozibul Haque @ Mozibur Rahman of Criminal Appeal No. 1448 of 1993 submits that the allegation against Mozibul Haque @ Mozibur Rahman was that he and another accused namely, Abdul Hakim @ Henju called out and took deceased Mozibul Haque @ Sahadat from their house at 7-00 PM on 9-10-1991 when Shahadat was reading and further allegation against him was that his name was disclosed in the confessional statements under section 164 CrPC (Exhibit 2, 2ka) of co-accused Abdul Hakim Henju and Md Ismail. 

 14. He then next argues that name of appellant Mozibul Haque @ Mozibur Rahman was mentioned in both Exhibit 2, 2ka statements under section 164 CrPC of accused Abdul Hakim Henju and Md Ismail. He contends that statement under section 164 CrPC even if be inculpatory, true and voluntary in nature can be used only against its maker and the same cannot be used against any co-accused unless there be any other corroborative evidence. He argues that except mere mention of the name of the appellant Mozibul Haque @ Mozibur Rahman there has been no other corroborative evidence in the record against the appellant and, as such, he submits that relying solely on Exhibit 2, 2ka there will be no legal scope for conviction of the appellant. He shows from the evidence on record that except mere mention of the name of the appellant there was no more corroborative evidence against the appellant. He accordingly, contends that the impugned order of conviction by the trial Court against this appellant Mozibul Haque @ Mozibur Rahman must be set aside as it was solely based on Exhibit 2, 2ka. In such regard he relies on the decision in the case of Ustar Ali vs State reported in 3 BLC (AD) 53 and 1998 BLD (AD) 43. Accordingly, he contends that Criminal Appeal No. 1448 of 1993 must succeed. 

 26. Learned Deputy Attorney-General submits in reply to contentions of the engaged Advocate for the appellant Mozibul Haque Mozibur Rahman that his name was duly disclosed in Exhibit 2, 2ka statements under section 164 CrPC of co-accused Abdul Hakim Henju and Md Ismail. He contends that above disclosure of his name in Exhibit 2 and 2ka but due assurance to the evidence of PW 4 Anwara Khaton who stated in her deposition that Mozibul Haque @ Mozibur Rahman and Abdul Hakim Henju called out deceased Sahadat Hossain from their house when Sahadat was reading at 7-00 PM on 9-10-1991 and they took him, evidence of PW 6 Fakir Ahmed who stated that at 7-00 PM on 9-10-1991 while he was returning from "Fazilar hat" he saw accused appellant Mozibul Haque with 3 others on culvert beside the house of informant Abdur Razzaque. He also shows from evidence of PW 9 Md Ismail and PW 13 Kefayetullah who stated that they saw in the night of 9-10-1991 Mozib, Abdul Hakim Henju and Sahadat were about to enter into the tea stall of PW 9 Md Ismail but when PW 13 Kefayetullah told Sahadat that his brother Ahsanullah was inside the tea stall, then they all went away. Thereafter Sahadat was killed. Learned Deputy Attorney-General submits that before occurrence deceased Sahadat was seen last in the company of appellant Mozibul Haque @ Mozibur Rahman and Abdul Hakim Henju. Learned Deputy Attorney-General accordingly submits that Exhibit 2, 2ka duly lent assurance to above circumstances disclosed in the evidence of PW 4, 6, 9 and 13 as above and as such according to learned Deputy Attorney-General the decision by the trial Court against appellant Mozibul Haque @ Mozibur Rahman of Criminal Appeal No. 1448 of 1993 can not be set aside and appeal must fail. 

 31. Learned Deputy Attorney-General relies on decisions reported in 2000 BLD 45 = 5 BLC 290 [State vs Billal Hossain], 44 DLR (AD) 51 [Hazrat Ali vs State], 5 BLC 332 [State vs Romana Begum @ Nomi], 7 BLT 41. Accordingly both Criminal Appeal No. 1448 of 1993 and 1685 of 1993 must fail. 

 36. It is true that in the case no eye-witness to the occurrence could be available. Two accused namely, Abdul Hakim @ Henju and Md Ismail made confessional statements under section 164 CrPC Exhibit 2, 2ka recorded by Magistrate Abu Taher PW 11. The said Exhibit 2, 2ka contained mention of the names of some accused namely, Mozibul Hoque @ Mozibur Rahman (appellant of Criminal Appeal No. 1448 of 1993) Rafique, Momin and Rahimullah acquitted, accused respondents of Criminal Appeal 4-94 preferred by State, Besides above disclosure of names of those above accused some circumstances came forth in evidence of PWs 4, 5, 6 and 13 against appellant of Criminal Appeal No. 1448 of 1993 (Mozibur Rahman), against appellant of Criminal Appeal No. 1685 of 1993 (Abdul Hakim @ Henju and Md Ismail and against acquittal accused Respondents Rafique, Momen and Rahimullah of Criminal Appeal 4 of 1994 preferred by State. 

 47. It therefore, appears that there has been no reliable substantive corroborative evidence against convict-appellant Mozibul Haque @ Mozibur Rahman of Criminal Appeal 1448 of 1993 and acquitted accused respondents Rafique, Momin and Rahimullah of Criminal Appeal 4 of 1994 (preferred by State) except Exhibit 2, 2ka of confessing accused-appellants Ismail of Criminal Appeal No. 1685 of 1993 disclosing names of those above co-accused and according to above decision Exhibit 2, 2ka cannot be used against those other co-accused under section 30 Evidence Act. Exhibit 2, 2ka can only lend assurance to other corroborative evidence if any in order to arrive at decision against other co-accused. Since in above scrutiny it transpires that other circumstances came forth in evidence have been found to be not reliable and sustainable due to inherent infirmity. Exhibit, 2-2ka can have no scope to lend assurance to any evidence against those co-accused as above. Obviously that above co-accused cannot be legally affected by Exhibit 2, 2ka in the absence of any other sufficient substantive corroborative evidence and thus they would be entitled to get benefit of doubt. In such regard reference may be made to the decision in the case of Dr Ishaque Ali vs State reported in 1993 BLD 236 wherein it was held as below; 

 57. Similarly, the cited decision in the case of State vs Raja A Majid and others reported in 1 BLC 144 cannot also be applicable in the present case as we already noticed that there was no non compliance of the provisions of section 164(3) CrPC by recording Magistrate in the present case. It was argued on behalf of appellants of Criminal Appeal 1685 of 1993 that manner of the occurrence was stated in one way in Exhibit 2 by accused Abdul Hakim @ Henju and in different way in Exhibit 2ka by accused Md Ismail. 

 81. We found earlier that except disclosure of the name of accused-appellant Mozibul Haque @ Mozibur Rahman in Exhibit 2 2ka by the confessing accused no other reliable substantive corroborative evidence came forth in evidence at the trial against him (Mozibur Rahman) and as such his conviction cannot be sustainable in law. Criminal Appeal 1448 of 1993 accordingly will succeed having merit in it. 

 86. Criminal Appeal No. 1448/93 is allowed. Impugned judgment, order of conviction and sentence dated 15-7-93 by the trial Court are set aside. Convict-appellant Mozibul Haque @ Mozibor Rahman is found not guilty of the offence under sections 302/34 Penal Code and he is accordingly acquitted of the charge thereunder. Appellant Mozibul Haque @ Mozibur Rahman (since on bail) is directed to be set at liberty if not connected with any other case. His bail bond be discharged.
